problem_text:
A corporate office must devise a procurement and storage strategy for an essential office supply over a workweek spanning 8 business days.  
The starting stock at the opening of the planning interval is 18 boxes.  
In each day \( t = 1, \dots, 8 \), the vendor permits the office to submit a requisition whose size must be between 11 and 49 boxes.  
Nevertheless, every requisition submitted will take 0 day(s) for delivery before it becomes available to meet consumption or restock the supply closet.  
The consumption of the office supply on each day is listed below:  
* Day 1: consumption 59 boxes  
* Day 2: consumption 36 boxes  
* Day 3: consumption 37 boxes  
* Day 4: consumption 21 boxes  
* Day 5: consumption 25 boxes  
* Day 6: consumption 39 boxes  
* Day 7: consumption 31 boxes  
* Day 8: consumption 43 boxes  

Stock‑outs are tolerated, but any unsatisfied consumption will not be carried forward.  
Throughout the 8‑day interval, supply quantities may be fractional, and the total volume of items physically present in the storage closet at any moment must not surpass the capacity limit of 29 boxes.

On the final day (day 8), the maximum requisition size is restricted to 40 boxes.  
On the first day, the physical stock on hand must be no less than 6 boxes.

The aggregate expense over the planning horizon comprises three elements: the procurement expense, which amounts to 4 per box requisitioned; the storage expense, which amounts to 1 per box kept overnight; and the shortage penalty, which amounts to 10 per box of unmet consumption. Determine the optimal requisition size for each day and monitor the resulting stock levels and shortage amounts in order to minimize the total expense.
